Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

message.content:
Below is a quick‑reference guide to the most popular “startup‑stat” APIs you can use to pull data about companies, funding rounds, valuations, employee counts, etc.  
I’ve grouped them by **access model** (free vs. paid), **data focus**, and **typical use‑case**.  For each API I include:

| API | What it offers | Typical auth | Example endpoint | Quick code snippet |
|-----|----------------|--------------|------------------|--------------------|
| **Crunchbase Public API** | Company profiles, funding, acquisitions, people | API key (free tier 100 req/day) | `/v3.1/organizations/{org_id}` | `GET https://api.crunchbase.com/v3.1/organizations/stripe?user_key=YOUR_KEY` |
| **Crunchbase Pro API** | Same as above + deeper analytics, custom queries | OAuth2 / API key (paid) | `/v3.1/organizations/{org_id}` | `GET https://api.crunchbase.com/v3.1/organizations/stripe?user_key=YOUR_KEY` |
| **AngelList GraphQL** | Startups, jobs, investors, funding | OAuth2 (GitHub/Google) | `https://api.angel.co/1/graphql` | `POST https://api.angel.co/1/graphql` with GraphQL query |
| **PitchBook API** | Private company data, M&A, VC, PE | Enterprise contract | `/companies/{id}` | `GET https://api.pitchbook.com/v1/companies/12345` |
| **CB Insights API** | Market intelligence, funding, exits | Enterprise contract | `/companies/{ticker}` | `GET https://api.cbinsights.com/v1/companies/stripe` |
| **DataFox (Oracle)** | Company fundamentals, funding, tech stack | Enterprise contract | `/companies/{id}` | `GET https://api.datafox.com/v1/companies/12345` |
| **OpenCorporates API** | Company registration, filings | Free tier 10 k req/month | `/companies/{jurisdiction}/{company_number}` | `GET https://api.opencorporates.com/v0.4/companies/gb/12345678` |
| **Open Data – Crunchbase** | Raw CSV dumps (free) | No auth | `https://data.crunchbase.com/downloads/companies.csv` | `GET https://data.crunchbase.com/downloads/companies.csv` |
| **Startup Genome API** | Startup ecosystem metrics | API key (free) | `/api/v1/startups/{id}` | `GET https://api.startupgenome.com/api/v1/startups/stripe?api_key=YOUR_KEY` |
| **S&P Capital IQ** | Company financials, valuations | Enterprise contract | `/companies/{ticker}` | `GET https://api.capitaliq.com/v1/companies/stripe` |

---

## How to Pick the Right API

| Need | Recommended API | Why |
|------|-----------------|-----|
| **Broad coverage, easy start** | Crunchbase Public | 100 req/day free, simple REST |
| **Deep funding & investor data** | Crunchbase Pro / PitchBook | Enterprise‑grade, richer fields |
| **GraphQL flexibility** | AngelList | Pull exactly what you need in one call |
| **Open‑source / free bulk data** | OpenCorporates / Crunchbase CSV | No auth, large datasets |
| **Valuation & market intelligence** | CB Insights / Startup Genome | Focus on valuation, ecosystem metrics |

---

## Quick‑Start Example (Python)

Below is a minimal example that pulls a company’s funding history from Crunchbase Public.  
Replace `YOUR_CRUNCHBASE_KEY` with your actual key.

```python
import requests

CRUNCHBASE_URL = "https://api.crunchbase.com/v3.1/organizations"
ORG_ID = "stripe"          # slug or UUID
API_KEY = "YOUR_CRUNCHBASE_KEY"

params = {
    "user_key": API_KEY,
    "include": "funding_rounds"   # optional: include related objects
}

resp = requests.get(f"{CRUNCHBASE_URL}/{ORG_ID}", params=params)
resp.raise_for_status()
data = resp.json()

print("Company:", data["data"]["organization"]["name"])
print("Funding rounds:")
for fr in data["data"]["organization"]["relationships"]["funding_rounds"]["items"]:
    print(f"  - {fr['name']} ({fr['funding_round']['funding_type']})")
```

---

## Authentication Tips

| API | Auth type | How to get it |
|-----|-----------|---------------|
| Crunchbase | API key | Sign up at crunchbase.com, go to “API” section |
| AngelList | OAuth2 | Create an app on angel.co, use GitHub/Google login |
| PitchBook / CB Insights | Enterprise | Contact sales, they’ll give you a token |
| OpenCorporates | None | Public endpoints, no key needed |
| Startup Genome | API key | Sign up at startupgenome.com, request key |

---

## Rate‑Limiting & Pagination

| API | Rate limit | Pagination |
|-----|------------|------------|
| Crunchbase Public | 100 req/day | `page` & `per_page` query params |
| Crunchbase Pro | 10 000 req/day | Same as above |
| AngelList | 200 req/min | `page` & `per_page` |
| PitchBook | 5 000 req/day | Cursor‑based |
| OpenCorporates | 10 k req/month | `page` & `per_page` |

Always check the docs for the exact limits; they can change.

---

## Common Use‑Cases

| Use‑Case | API | Sample Query |
|----------|-----|--------------|
| **Build a startup discovery app** | Crunchbase Public | `GET /organizations?query=AI&location=San+Francisco` |
| **Track funding rounds over time** | Crunchbase Pro | `GET /organizations/{id}/funding_rounds` |
| **Match startups to investors** | AngelList GraphQL | `{ startups(filter:{investor:"sequoia"}){name, fundingRounds{amount}} }` |
| **Generate valuation heatmaps** | CB Insights | `GET /companies/{ticker}/valuation` |
| **Export bulk company list** | Crunchbase CSV | Download `companies.csv` |

---

## Next Steps

1. **Decide on scope** – Do you need just company names or deep funding data?
2. **Check pricing** – Free tiers are great for prototyping; enterprise plans unlock richer data.
3. **Register & get keys** – Follow the auth instructions above.
4. **Start coding** – Use the snippets as a template.

If you need help writing a specific query or handling pagination, let me know!
